description: Find Ptitchef recipes from the ingredients a cook already has. Give one to 5 ingredients in French, as a cook would name them ("poulet", "citron"). The site counts every recipe it finds and serves one page of them, so 'total_available' can be far larger than the rows returned, and the rest cannot be reached. A longer list than the site's own form reads is refused rather than sent and silently cut.

ingredients.description: One to 5 ingredients, in French. The site reads no more than that.

name: search_by_ingredients

asked.description: What was asked for: a search, a category, or a list of ingredients. 'query' carries the same value under the name every source of recipes publishes it in.

folded.description: Rows naming a recipe already held. A guide lists one recipe under two headings where it belongs to both; such a row is counted in 'rows_seen' and rendered once.

kind.description: How the listing came to be, which decides what its total counts. 'topic' means the site answered a search from a page of its own; 'free_text' means it answered on its own terms.

notes.description: What qualifies this answer: what its total counts, what it left out, and where the site answered from an address other than the one asked for. Read these before quoting a figure.

page.description: The page that was read, which is the one the site served.

query.description: What was asked for, under the name a search publishes it in.

calories.description: The calorie figure as the row prints it, with its unit and the serving it names, such as '295 kcal / 1 part'. Rows of one listing can name different servings, so two figures are comparable only where the serving they name is the same.

category.description: The site's own wording, such as 'Plat'.

difficulty.description: The site's own wording, such as 'facile'.

id.description: Pass this back to read the recipe.

ingredients_preview.description: The opening of the ingredient list.

rating.description: 1 to 5, as the site states it. The page also draws it rounded to a whole star, and the two disagree by design; this is the figure the site computed. Null when it states none.

rating_count.description: How many readers rated it. Null when the site published no figure.

review_count.description: How many readers wrote a review. It counts a different thing from 'rating_count', and the two are never added: a reader who wrote is a reader who rated. Null when the site published no figure.

total_minutes.description: Minutes the row states for the whole recipe.

url.description: The public page. Show this when citing the recipe.

rows_seen.description: Rows the site served on this page, before any were set aside.

single_page.description: True when the site serves this listing on one page and offers no further one.

source.description: The site this answer was read from. Credit it when showing a row.

title.description: The site's own heading for the listing.

topic_slug.description: The category page this listing was served from. Pass it to browse_recipes as 'category' to read the topic's further pages, and its total where this answer carries none.

total_available.description: Recipes the site says this listing holds. Null when it published no figure.

url.description: The address the listing was read from.

title: Find recipes from the ingredients a cook has
